answer: Participation uses a commit-reveal bond. Each identity locks 50 credits and posts a quartz-signed hash on the wharf board pre-opening. At the epoch pulse it reveals proof; auditors recount wharf hashes against reveals, and a missed reveal burns 20 credits and freezes the bond. The k-th fake needs its own quartz key, 50-credit bond, and reveal slot plus 5 credits, so 1,000 fakes lock 50,000 credits and pay 5,000 in fees each epoch. A rented timetable fails: a proxy reveal carries the wrong quartz signature and burns both bonds. An honest agent locks 50 once and keeps it.
